data.title: Will Solid Power (NASDAQ:SLDP) Spend Its Cash Wisely?
data.description:
We can readily understand why investors are attracted to unprofitable companies. For example, although Amazon.com made losses for many years after listing, if you had bought and held the shares since 1999, you would have made a fortune. But while the successes are well known, investors should not ignore the very many unprofitable companies that simply burn through all their cash and collapse.

So should Solid Power (NASDAQ:SLDP) shareholders be worried about its cash burn? For the purpose of this article, we'll define cash burn as the amount of cash the company is spending each year to fund its growth (also called its negative free cash flow). We'll start by comparing its cash burn with its cash reserves in order to calculate its cash runway.

How Long Is Solid Power's Cash Runway?

A company's cash runway is calculated by dividing its cash hoard by its cash burn. When Solid Power last reported its September 2026 balance sheet in November 2026, it had zero debt and cash worth US$235m. Importantly, its cash burn was US$80m over the trailing twelve months. Therefore, from September 2026 it had 2.9 years of cash runway. Arguably, that's a prudent and sensible length of runway to have. The image below shows how its cash balance has been changing over the last few years.

Check out our latest analysis for Solid Power

How Well Is Solid Power Growing?

Over the last year, Solid Power maintained its cash burn at a fairly steady level. However, if you like growth, you might be turned off the stock by the dizzying decline in operating revenue, which is down 80% year on year. In light of the above-mentioned, we're pretty wary of the trajectory the company seems to be on. Clearly, however, the crucial factor is whether the company will grow its business going forward. So you might want to take a peek at how much the company is expected to grow in the next few years.

How Easily Can Solid Power Raise Cash?

While Solid Power seems to be in a fairly good position, it's still worth considering how easily it could raise more cash, even just to fuel faster growth. Issuing new shares, or taking on debt, are the most common ways for a listed company to raise more money for its business. Commonly, a business will sell new shares in itself to raise cash and drive growth. We can compare a company's cash burn to its market capitalisation to get a sense for how many new shares a company would have to issue to fund one year's operations.

Since it has a market capitalisation of US$358m, Solid Power's US$80m in cash burn equates to about 22% of its market value. That's not insignificant, and if the company had to sell enough shares to fund another year's growth at the current share price, you'd likely witness fairly costly dilution.

So, Should We Worry About Solid Power's Cash Burn?

On this analysis of Solid Power's cash burn, we think its cash runway was reassuring, while its falling revenue has us a bit worried. Even though we don't think it has a problem with its cash burn, the analysis we've done in this article does suggest that shareholders should give some careful thought to the potential cost of raising more money in the future. data.title: Concerns Surrounding Hudbay Minerals' (TSE:HBM) Performance
data.description:
The market shrugged off Hudbay Minerals Inc.'s (TSE:HBM) solid earnings report. We think that investors might be worried about some concerning underlying factors.

This technology could replace computers: discover the 20 stocks are working to make quantum computing a reality.

To understand the value of a company's earnings growth, it is imperative to consider any dilution of shareholders' interests. As it happens, Hudbay Minerals issued 12% more new shares over the last year. Therefore, each share now receives a smaller portion of profit. Per share metrics like EPS help us understand how much actual shareholders are benefitting from the company's profits, while the net income level gives us a better view of the company's absolute size. You can see a chart of Hudbay Minerals' EPS by clicking here.

How Is Dilution Impacting Hudbay Minerals' Earnings Per Share (EPS)?

As you can see above, Hudbay Minerals has been growing its net income over the last few years, with an annualized gain of 3,224% over three years. But EPS was only up 2,292% per year, in the exact same period. And at a glance the 31% gain in profit over the last year impresses. On the other hand, earnings per share are only up 30% in that time. And so, you can see quite clearly that dilution is influencing shareholder earnings.

In the long term, earnings per share growth should beget share price growth. So it will certainly be a positive for shareholders if Hudbay Minerals can grow EPS persistently. But on the other hand, we'd be far less excited to learn profit (but not EPS) was improving. For that reason, you could say that EPS is more important that net income in the long run, assuming the goal is to assess whether a company's share price might grow.

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

How Do Unusual Items Influence Profit?

Finally, we should also consider the fact that unusual items boosted Hudbay Minerals' net profit by US$81m over the last year. While we like to see profit increases, we tend to be a little more cautious when unusual items have made a big contribution. When we crunched the numbers on thousands of publicly listed companies, we found that a boost from unusual items in a given year is often not repeated the next year. And that's as you'd expect, given these boosts are described as 'unusual'. If Hudbay Minerals doesn't see that contribution repeat, then all else being equal we'd expect its profit to drop over the current year.

Our Take On Hudbay Minerals' Profit Performance

In its last report Hudbay Minerals benefitted from unusual items which boosted its profit, which could make the profit seem better than it really is on a sustainable basis. On top of that, the dilution means that its earnings per share performance is worse than its profit performance. Considering all this we'd argue Hudbay Minerals' profits probably give an overly generous impression of its sustainable level of profitability. While it's really important to consider how well a company's statutory earnings represent its true earnings power, it's also worth taking a look at what analysts are forecasting for the future. data.title: Is MiNK Therapeutics (NASDAQ:INKT) In A Good Position To Deliver On Growth Plans?
data.description:
Just because a business does not make any money, does not mean that the stock will go down. For example, although software-as-a-service business Salesforce.com lost money for years while it grew recurring revenue, if you held shares since 2005, you'd have done very well indeed. But while the successes are well known, investors should not ignore the very many unprofitable companies that simply burn through all their cash and collapse.

So should MiNK Therapeutics (NASDAQ:INKT) shareholders be worried about its cash burn? The first step is to compare its cash burn with its cash reserves, to give us its 'cash runway'.

Does MiNK Therapeutics Have A Long Cash Runway?

A cash runway is defined as the length of time it would take a company to run out of money if it kept spending at its current rate of cash burn. As at September 2026, MiNK Therapeutics had cash of US$7.5m and no debt. In the last year, its cash burn was US$7.2m. So it had a cash runway of approximately 12 months from September 2026. While that cash runway isn't too concerning, sensible holders would be peering into the distance, and considering what happens if the company runs out of cash. Therefore, for the purposes of this analysis we'll focus on how the cash burn is tracking. With the cash burn rate up 29% in the last year, it seems that the company is ratcheting up investment in the business over time. That's not necessarily a bad thing, but investors should be mindful of the fact that will shorten the cash runway. While the past is always worth studying, it is the future that matters most of all. How Hard Would It Be For MiNK Therapeutics To Raise More Cash For Growth?

While MiNK Therapeutics does have a solid cash runway, its cash burn trajectory may have some shareholders thinking ahead to when the company may need to raise more cash. Generally speaking, a listed business can raise new cash through issuing shares or taking on debt. Many companies end up issuing new shares to fund future growth. By comparing a company's annual cash burn to its total market capitalisation, we can estimate roughly how many shares it would have to issue in order to run the company for another year (at the same burn rate).

MiNK Therapeutics has a market capitalisation of US$47m and burnt through US$7.2m last year, which is 15% of the company's market value. Given that situation, it's fair to say the company wouldn't have much trouble raising more cash for growth, but shareholders would be somewhat diluted.

How Risky Is MiNK Therapeutics' Cash Burn Situation?

ReposiTrak beat revenue forecasts by a solid 16% to hit US$5.8m. Statutory earnings per share came in at US$0.08, in line with expectations. Following the result, the analyst has updated their earnings model, and it would be good to know whether they think there's been a strong change in the company's prospects, or if it's business as usual. If met, this would reflect a meaningful 14% improvement in revenue compared to the last 12 months. Statutory per share are forecast to be US$0.39, approximately in line with the last 12 months. Yet prior to the latest earnings, the analyst had been anticipated revenues of US$25.5m and earnings per share (EPS) of US$0.43 in 2027. Overall it looks as though the analyst was a bit mixed on the latest results. Although there was a a meaningful to revenue, the consensus also made a small dip in its earnings per share forecasts.

The analyst also cut ReposiTrak's price target 45% to US$16.00, implying that lower forecast earnings are expected to have a more negative impact than can be offset by the increase in revenue.

The analyst is definitely expecting ReposiTrak's growth to accelerate, with the forecast 19% annualised growth to the end of 2027 ranking favourably alongside historical growth of 5.4% per annum over the past five years. Other similar companies in the industry (with analyst coverage) are also forecast to grow their revenue at 17% per year. Factoring in the forecast acceleration in revenue, it's pretty clear that ReposiTrak is expected to grow at about the same rate as the wider industry.

The Bottom Line

The biggest concern is that the analyst reduced their earnings per share estimates, suggesting business headwinds could lay ahead for ReposiTrak. There was also an upgrade to revenue estimates, although as we saw earlier, forecast growth is only expected to be about the same as the wider industry. Furthermore, the analyst also cut their price targets, suggesting that the latest news has led to greater pessimism about the intrinsic value of the business.

The current metals sell off and cost guidance reset put near term focus on cash generation and discipline rather than pure volume growth.

The key short term catalyst is how Newmont executes through rising 2027 development spending and inflation without eroding margins too sharply. The biggest risk sits in capital intensity, from Red Chris to projects like Lihir, where any delays, safety issues or further cost creep would pressure free cash flow and investor confidence.

The most relevant fresh datapoint is the August 2026 Blue Lake Penstock Repair Project construction report filed with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission. It may look like a small hydro related footnote, yet it reinforces that Newmont is working through a series of infrastructure and legacy assets that all feed into operating reliability and regulatory relationships.

For you as an investor, that filing sits alongside the cost outlook and the metals pullback as part of the same story. Execution on projects like Blue Lake and Red Chris, together with the higher capex and inflation risks highlighted in the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St, will shape whether Newmont turns its large project pipeline into stable production rather than recurring interruptions.

Analysts are effectively baking in both higher profit margins and a larger top line, with expectations that margins move from 34.7% today to 37.8% in three years. For you as a shareholder, that combination matters more than any single production target because it speaks directly to how much of every future gold and copper dollar might actually reach the bottom line.

The earnings ramp also comes with a wide spread of opinions. Forecasts cluster around US$11.9b in profit by 2029, but the range runs from US$9.5b to US$14.3b. That disagreement indicates that the path from today’s operations, through projects like Red Chris and the cost reset, to those future numbers is anything but straightforward.

In addition, the analyst framework assumes Newmont shrinks its share count by about 4.77% per year for the next three years. If that happens, per share figures would benefit even if absolute earnings only track the mid range of forecasts. If buybacks slow or pause because of higher capex or weaker metals pricing, that per share uplift would look very different.

Valuation work in these reports ties the 2029 earnings line to a P/E of 13.2x, slightly below the current multiple of 13.6x and also below the cited 15.5x for the wider US metals and mining industry. In this framework, analysts appear comfortable with Newmont earning a modest discount to peers while still ramping profit over time.

Some forecasters stretch to US$165.00, while the most cautious come in at US$70.00, which underlines how sensitive this story is to execution on costs, capital projects and movements in metals prices.

For anyone tracking Newmont after the recent metals sell off, these metrics provide a clear checklist. Revenue growing near 5.7% a year, earnings stepping from US$9.2b to a potential US$11.9b, margins edging higher and the share count declining all need to align for the analyst case to hold together.

data.title: There May Be Reason For Hope In MT Højgaard Holding's (CPH:MTHH) Disappointing Earnings
data.description:
The market was pleased with the recent earnings report from MT Højgaard Holding A/S (CPH:MTHH), despite the profit numbers being soft. Our analysis suggests that investors may have noticed some promising signs beyond the statutory profit figures.

This technology could replace computers: discover the 20 stocks are working to make quantum computing a reality.

Examining Cashflow Against MT Højgaard Holding's Earnings

Many investors haven't heard of the accrual ratio from cashflow, but it is actually a useful measure of how well a company's profit is backed up by free cash flow (FCF) during a given period. In plain english, this ratio subtracts FCF from net profit, and divides that number by the company's average operating assets over that period. This ratio tells us how much of a company's profit is not backed by free cashflow.

As a result, a negative accrual ratio is a positive for the company, and a positive accrual ratio is a negative. While it's not a problem to have a positive accrual ratio, indicating a certain level of non-cash profits, a high accrual ratio is arguably a bad thing, because it indicates paper profits are not matched by cash flow. That's because some academic studies have suggested that high accruals ratios tend to lead to lower profit or less profit growth.

Over the twelve months to September 2026, MT Højgaard Holding recorded an accrual ratio of -0.14. That implies it has good cash conversion, and implies that its free cash flow solidly exceeded its profit last year. To wit, it produced free cash flow of kr.238m during the period, dwarfing its reported profit of kr.152.5m. MT Højgaard Holding's free cash flow actually declined over the last year, which is disappointing, like non-biodegradable balloons.

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

Our Take On MT Højgaard Holding's Profit Performance

As we discussed above, MT Højgaard Holding has perfectly satisfactory free cash flow relative to profit. Because of this, we think MT Højgaard Holding's earnings potential is at least as good as it seems, and maybe even better! Unfortunately, though, its earnings per share actually fell back over the last year. Of course, we've only just scratched the surface when it comes to analysing its earnings; one could also consider margins, forecast growth, and return on investment, among other factors. So if you'd like to dive deeper into this stock, it's crucial to consider any risks it's facing. Case in point: We've spotted 2 warning signs for MT Højgaard Holding you should be aware of.

Only 32.4% of the portfolio is in capital markets industries, with the rest spread across diversified banks, insurance groups and other financials, so the direct effect of a single listing is cushioned by plenty of businesses tied to lending, premiums and fee income.

Simply Wall St estimates that 84.1% of this ETF by weight is in holdings trading below its assessment of fair value. This may interest investors who want the capital markets angle without giving up wider financials exposure. That mix leaves you leaning on a big pair of banks and a broad set of insurers, asset managers and exchanges to share the load, but it also means Anthropic related activity is only one of several forces likely to drive the fund over time.

The exposure trade-off

If you want the Anthropic IPO front and centre, IAI and KCE are the closest fit. IAI leans hardest on a few large banks and exchanges, with Goldman Sachs alone carrying the highest single weight of the trio. KCE spreads that same theme over more holdings, so Donnelley Financial Solutions, Tradeweb Markets and others each play a smaller part. Underwriters and trading platforms need to keep a strong grip on allocations and aftermarket activity for this to matter.

IYF turns the dial down. Only 32.4% of the fund sits in capital markets, with the rest in broader banking and insurance. Berkshire Hathaway and JPMorgan Chase connect you to Anthropic related activity, yet much of the ETF is driven by lending, balance sheet strength and insurance premiums instead. IAI has the highest share of holdings below Simply Wall St fair value estimates, KCE the lowest and IYF the highest of all three. data.title: We Think You Can Look Beyond Trade Desk's (NASDAQ:TTD) Lackluster Earnings
data.description:
The Trade Desk, Inc.'s (NASDAQ:TTD) stock was strong despite it releasing a soft earnings report last week. We think that investors might be looking at some positive factors beyond the earnings numbers.

This technology could replace computers: discover the 20 stocks are working to make quantum computing a reality.

Examining Cashflow Against Trade Desk's Earnings

Many investors haven't heard of the accrual ratio from cashflow, but it is actually a useful measure of how well a company's profit is backed up by free cash flow (FCF) during a given period. In plain english, this ratio subtracts FCF from net profit, and divides that number by the company's average operating assets over that period. This ratio tells us how much of a company's profit is not backed by free cashflow.

Therefore, it's actually considered a good thing when a company has a negative accrual ratio, but a bad thing if its accrual ratio is positive. While it's not a problem to have a positive accrual ratio, indicating a certain level of non-cash profits, a high accrual ratio is arguably a bad thing, because it indicates paper profits are not matched by cash flow. That's because some academic studies have suggested that high accruals ratios tend to lead to lower profit or less profit growth.

For the year to September 2026, Trade Desk had an accrual ratio of -0.47. That indicates that its free cash flow quite significantly exceeded its statutory profit. To wit, it produced free cash flow of US$847m during the period, dwarfing its reported profit of US$329.4m. Trade Desk shareholders are no doubt pleased that free cash flow improved over the last twelve months.

Our Take On Trade Desk's Profit Performance

Happily for shareholders, Trade Desk produced plenty of free cash flow to back up its statutory profit numbers. Based on this observation, we consider it possible that Trade Desk's statutory profit actually understates its earnings potential! And on top of that, its earnings per share have grown at an extremely impressive rate over the last three years.
